HERO_SUBHEAD: Your agent's prompts, tools, and models change weekly. Your users deserve to know. Hosted changelog + RSS + embed widget in 60 seconds.
PROBLEM_STATEMENT: You changed the system prompt, swapped the retrieval model, or deprecated a tool — and now half your users are confused. GitHub Releases is for code; users don't have GitHub accounts. A Notion page is a broken link waiting to happen. Agent Changelog is a hosted page that stays live forever.
FEATURE_1_BODY: Write releases in Markdown. Sections: Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security. Auto-parsed for the embed widget.
FEATURE_2_BODY: One-line <script> tag drops a 'What's new?' popover in your agent's UI. RSS feed for developers who follow you.
FEATURE_3_BODY: Bump the major version and subscribed users get an email. No email-list plumbing on your side — we ship the whole thing.

FAQ_1_Q: How do I post a release?
FAQ_1_A: Three ways: (1) paste Markdown in the dashboard, (2) POST to /api/releases with a bearer token, or (3) GitHub Action watches a CHANGELOG.md in your repo and syncs on push.
FAQ_2_Q: Does the embed widget work in any framework?
FAQ_2_A: Yes. It's one <script> tag, no framework dependency. Shadow-DOM'd so it can't collide with your CSS. React / Vue / Svelte wrappers are optional but not required.
FAQ_3_Q: Why not just use a Notion page?
FAQ_3_A: Notion pages break, get de-indexed, and don't offer RSS. This is a purpose-built static changelog with SEO, semver semantics, and a permanent URL. Costs less than one Notion seat.
FAQ_4_Q: Can users subscribe by email without an account?
FAQ_4_A: Yes, on Pro. Double-opt-in email capture on your changelog page. We handle bounces and unsubscribes. GDPR / CAN-SPAM compliant.
